meta.note: RENAMED TWICE: Dataplex became Dataplex Universal Catalog, then Knowledge Catalog on 10 April 2026. Google states the API, client library, CLI and IAM names are unchanged and that discovery, lineage, data quality and business glossaries are unaffected — so, like BigLake, this is presentational and existing code stays valid. Slug kept as dataplex; the docs themselves still live under /dataplex/docs.

name: Knowledge Catalog
oneLiner: Unified catalog, governance and quality across your lakes and warehouses.
whatItIs: Dataplex is Google Cloud's data-governance and management fabric. It lets you organise data spread across Cloud Storage buckets and BigQuery datasets into logical lakes and zones, automatically catalogs and profiles it, and applies governance — access policies, data quality checks and lineage — consistently across it all. It now incorporates Data Catalog for search/metadata. Where BigLake enforces fine-grained access, Dataplex is the higher-level control plane that discovers, describes, governs and monitors the quality of your data estate so people can find and trust it.

inPractice.narrative: A company's data is scattered across many GCS buckets and BigQuery datasets. An admin defines Dataplex lakes and zones that logically group them by domain, and Dataplex auto-discovers tables, harvests metadata into the catalog, runs data-quality scans, and tracks lineage. Analysts search the catalog to find trustworthy datasets; policies applied in Dataplex (enforced via BigLake) govern access. It's the map-and-rulebook over an otherwise sprawling estate.

coreConcepts.detail: Logical containers that group physical data (GCS/BigQuery) by domain and refine it into zones (e.g. raw vs curated), independent of where bytes physically live.
Auto-discovers assets and harvests technical + business metadata into a searchable catalog, so users can find datasets across the estate.
Built-in scans profile data and run quality rules (nulls, ranges, uniqueness), surfacing scores and issues without a separate tool.
Central access and data policies applied across grouped assets, enforced together with BigLake for fine-grained control.
Tracks how data flows and transforms across BigQuery/Dataflow/etc., aiding trust, debugging and impact analysis.
Classify and tag data (e.g. PII) to drive policy and discovery at scale rather than per-table management.

whenToUse: Governing and cataloguing data spread across GCS and BigQuery centrally.
Making datasets discoverable and trustworthy for analysts (search + metadata).
Automated data-quality profiling and rule checks across the estate.
Applying consistent policies and classification at scale.
Tracking lineage for governance and impact analysis.
whenNotToUse: A tiny single-dataset project where a catalog/governance layer is overkill.
Purely enforcing table access with nothing else — BigLake alone may suffice.
Non-GCP data estates as the primary target — it's GCP-centric.
Real-time data processing — it's governance/management, not a pipeline engine.

source.quote: Dataplex Universal Catalog is now called Knowledge Catalog. … Knowledge Catalog is a Gemini-powered data catalog that provides universal business context and governance for your entire data estate.

keyFacts.label: Organises
keyFacts.value: Cloud Storage + BigQuery into logical lakes/zones.

keyFacts.label: Catalog
keyFacts.value: Catalog: absorbed Data Catalog; now the Knowledge Catalog metadata layer.

keyFacts.label: Enforcement
keyFacts.value: Policies applied with BigLake for fine-grained access.

pricingShape: Dataplex charges are largely usage-based: the data-processing it does for discovery, profiling and data-quality scans (billed by processing units/DCUs for the time those tasks run), plus catalog metadata storage/API usage. Organising data into lakes and zones itself is cheap; the cost grows with how much scanning and quality checking you run. Underlying storage (GCS/BigQuery) and query compute are separate. So the lever is how frequently and broadly you profile/scan versus governing metadata that changes slowly.
gotchas: Frequent quality/discovery scans over large data accrue processing cost — schedule them sensibly.
It's a management layer, not storage or compute — people expect a 'lake product' and it's really governance over existing data.
Effective use needs a domain/zone design up front; ad-hoc grouping undermines the value.
Fine-grained access enforcement leans on BigLake — Dataplex policies and BigLake need to line up.
The Data Catalog/Dataplex product boundaries have shifted over time; follow current docs for what lives where.
